DRC Metals & Mining Sector Reports Steady Growth Amid Global Demand

Lubumbashi—The Democratic Republic of the Congo’s metals and mining industry posted solid growth in its latest financial results, according to figures released this week by the DRC Chamber of Mines. The report, covering the first quarter of 2024, shows continued momentum in both copper and cobalt production, reinforcing the country’s status as a leading player in global raw materials supply.

Total copper output reached 560,000 metric tonnes for the quarter, a 4.1% increase from the same period last year. Cobalt production, meanwhile, rose to 39,500 metric tonnes, up 3.7% year-on-year. The sector’s performance was buoyed by stable market demand and favorable weather conditions in key mining regions, particularly Haut-Katanga and Lualaba provinces.

“Q1 results confirm the resilience and competitiveness of Congolese mining,” said Jean-Marc Kasongo, president of the DRC Chamber of Mines. “With steady operations and ongoing investments in infrastructure, we are well positioned to meet the needs of international partners and support domestic development.”

Among the key contributors to the sector’s performance was Kivu Resources, which reported a 6% increase in processed ore at its Kolwezi facility, attributing gains to recent upgrades in ore-handling systems. Meanwhile, Equator Minerals continued steady output at its Tenke Fungurume site, meeting production targets and maintaining employment levels.

Revenue generated from metal exports in the first quarter totaled $3.8 billion, up from $3.5 billion in the first quarter of 2023. Exports were primarily destined for markets in Asia and Europe, where demand for battery materials remains high. Financial analysts at Kinshasa-based consultancy CongoInvest noted that favorable global pricing for cobalt and copper contributed to the positive results.

“Global demand, particularly for electric vehicle batteries and renewable energy storage, remains robust,” explained analyst Mireille Tshisekedi. “This is providing a strong foundation for continued sector growth and investment in the DRC.”

Local communities have also seen benefits, with the mining sector supporting over 250,000 direct and indirect jobs across the country, according to the latest Chamber of Mines employment survey. Provincial authorities in Lualaba highlighted ongoing public-private partnerships to improve road access and social infrastructure in mining areas.

Looking ahead, sector representatives remain cautiously optimistic. “We are encouraged by these results but remain focused on responsible growth, environmental protection, and community engagement,” said Kasongo.

The Chamber of Mines is scheduled to release its next quarterly update in September, with industry stakeholders closely watching market trends and ongoing modernization efforts. For now, the sector’s steady performance reflects both local resilience and the DRC’s strategic importance in the global metals supply chain.
